text: Walking back from lunch, Akshit Parmar and Jacinth Jebaraj began talking about an idea. That conversation became the starting point for Élan, founded by Akshit with co-founders Sakshi Baldawa, Prachi Belagali and Jacinth.
The first Élan Summit took place at SGIS Pune Campus, Mulshi, on 5–6 September 2026. Across two days, the committee rooms and stage became the setting for our first chapter.
We wanted students to have a part in the event, not just a seat in the audience.

At the first Élan Summit, students formed cabinets, worked through business challenges and presented decisions they had made together. The sessions gave them a reason to speak up and listen to people from other schools.
Outside the committee rooms, there were performances, conversations and a DJ night. Those shared moments were part of what we wanted Élan to be.
Make leadership, creativity and collaboration something young people can practise together.
A nation in crisis. A cabinet under pressure. Work with your team, weigh the consequences and defend a response.
Build a brand or navigate a market. Bring strategy, creativity and judgement to a business arena that keeps changing.
In the 2026 edition, the two flagships ran in parallel. For the second edition, Crisis Command will be the sole flagship. Cent$ible remains part of our first-edition story.
What happens between the sessions matters too.
A stage for performance, a platform for ideas and the confidence to put something of your own into the world.
From cabinet decisions to organising and volunteering, students take ownership of work that affects other people.
Mixed-school teams, shared activities and conversations give people a reason to meet and work together.
The way people are welcomed, the spaces they share and the time between sessions all shape what they remember.

Pitch like a founder. Think like an investor. Two business themes lead to one final test: the decisions you can defend in the boardroom.

Cent$ible is a live inter-school business arena. Across two competitive themes, teams build brands and trade markets, and the best teams advance to the Boardroom Finale.
One arena, two themes, one champion.

Cent$ible is built around two business themes. Each one is its own competition with several rounds, and the strongest teams from every theme go through to the Boardroom Finale to fight for the overall championship.
You compete in teams in the theme you choose. Between the rounds there are networking sessions and interactive activities.
Open to school students aged 14 to 20, across schools and delegations. First-year university students within the same age range are also eligible and can register individually.
A shared in-event currency. Teams earn it, invest it, and bid with it as the rounds play out.
The top teams from each theme meet in the finale to decide the overall champion.

Build, adapt, pitch, and dominate. BRAND बनाओ is where you create a real startup and pitch it under pressure, with your idea evolving across three rounds the way it draws on Shark Tank, a startup expo, and live business decisions.

Two days before Élan, every team submits a short product information form: brand name, product or service, target customer, price range, business model, sales channel, key differentiator, one major dependency and your expansion idea. This is what the organising team uses to build a crisis tailored to your startup. You will not be told what that crisis is.

A five-minute pitch, delivered as founders speaking to investors. Cover your brand name and what it means, your logo and the thinking behind it, your target audience, your business model and how you make money, your marketing strategy, and your future vision. Judges may stop you at five minutes, so rehearse to the clock.

After lunch you receive a sealed envelope containing a crisis built specifically for your startup. You get twenty minutes to analyse it and rebuild your strategy, then three minutes to present your recovery plan: what happened, what you do first, what changes, how you protect customer trust, and how you prevent it happening again. The top three teams go through to the Boardroom.

Risk everything and survive the chaos. NOTE नीति is a live financial simulation where you trade, negotiate, ride out crashes, and make risky calls under pressure, working with real market situations instead of textbook problems.

Two hours on a live market run through the Élan portal. You invest your Cents across companies that rise and fall, and every five minutes the host announces a new market status: you hold, sell or switch. Your portfolio is valued live, the leaderboard moves with it, and when the final freeze is called your closing capital is locked.

The floor becomes physical. Every team is handed thirty coins, ten red, ten blue and ten black, and five zones open at once: Dice of Fortune, the Spin Wheel, Stock Market Dart, Investment Plinko and the Bull versus Bear Arena. You choose your own route, you may play any zone twice, and your team can split up to cover more ground. Ninety minutes, then the zones close and your coins are counted.
Your Round 1 closing capital is added to the value of the coins you finish with. The three teams holding the most combined capital go through to the Cent$ible Boardroom on Day 2.
Cent$ible sits between the classroom and the real business world, and it leans on the same skills a founder, a marketer, or an investor uses every day.
Turn ideas into ventures and defend them.
Read markets, manage risk, make the call.
Influence an audience and own a narrative.
Lead a team when the pressure is on.
Adapt fast when the brief changes.
Present, persuade, and pivot on your feet.
The three highest-scoring teams from every theme come together on Day 2 for the Boardroom Finale, the last stage of Cent$ible and the one that decides the overall championship.

The Boardroom stops being a quiz or a pitch and becomes a business decision-making arena. Finalists are given a business situation drawn from areas such as startup strategy, marketing, finance, brand management, business expansion, crisis management and entrepreneurial decision-making. You analyse the information, identify the opportunity, decide on a course of action, and then justify it to the board.

Judging covers business knowledge, strategic thinking, creativity, decision-making, problem-solving, financial understanding, communication, confidence, teamwork and composure under pressure. The challenge is built to separate a team that knows business concepts from a team that can actually think like business leaders.

Cent$ible is Élan’s business flagship, run in collaboration with Sanjay Ghodawat International School. It is a live inter-school business arena for students aged 14 to 20 where teams compete and collaborate across two themes, and the strongest teams advance to the Boardroom Finale.
Cent$ible is open to school students aged 14 to 20, across schools and delegations. First-year university students within the same age range are also eligible and can register individually.

It is team-based. Cent$ible is built around two competitive themes, and each theme is its own competition with two rounds. The strongest teams from every theme go through to the Boardroom Finale to compete for the overall championship, and there are networking sessions and interactive activities between rounds.
The two themes are BRAND बनाओ and NOTE नीति. Each theme runs its own rounds and sends its top three teams to the Boardroom Finale.
Cents are Cent$ible’s shared in-event currency. Teams earn, invest, and bid with Cents as the rounds play out.

The Boardroom Finale is the Day 2 round that decides the overall Cent$ible champion. The three highest-scoring teams from every theme come together and are given a business situation drawn from areas such as startup strategy, marketing, finance, brand management, business expansion, crisis management or entrepreneurial decision-making. Teams analyse the information, decide on a course of action, justify it to the board and answer board questioning. It is judged on business knowledge, strategic thinking, creativity, decision-making, problem-solving, financial understanding, communication, confidence, teamwork and composure under pressure.
No specific business background is required. Cent$ible is open to all students aged 14 to 20, and the rounds are built around creativity, strategy, adaptability, communication, and quick thinking.

BETWEEN THE BRIEF AND THE DECISION
The other side of our first edition.
Akshit founded Élan with co-founders Sakshi, Prachi and Jacinth. Here are the interests, conversations and people behind its first edition.
Chess, coastlines and a curiosity about the universe.

I’m Akshit Parmar, the founder of Élan and the Director of its 2026 edition. I enjoy chess, gaming and spending time at the beach. I’m also aiming to become an astrophysicist. I want to understand more about the universe and how it works.

Élan has been a dream project of mine. Getting to bring it to life made the first edition especially personal. More than anything, I hope everyone who joined us enjoyed being part of it and left with something they’ll remember fondly.
Curiosity in business. Creativity in expression.

Sakshi Baldawa is a co-founder of Élan Summit and served as Assistant Director of its 2026 edition. With a keen interest in finance, business and economics, she enjoys exploring new ideas, connecting with people and turning thought into action.

Dance is another expression of that curiosity and energy. Alongside her academic interests and leadership work, it gives her space to create and express herself. She enjoys working with others, taking initiative and learning as she goes.
One of the Heads of All Departments · Élan 2026
Curious about people, perspectives and the questions in between.

I’m Prachi Belagali. I’m drawn to law and history, especially the questions they raise about people: what shapes our beliefs, why we think differently, and how another perspective can change our own. Outside academics, Taekwondo has been a big part of my life, teaching me discipline, resilience and the importance of showing up when things get difficult.

I’ve never believed learning ends at the classroom door. Some of my most meaningful lessons have come from conversations, disagreements and experiences that challenged what I thought I knew. I’m still figuring things out, and I enjoy that uncertainty.

As a co-founder of Élan and one of the Heads of All Departments for its 2026 edition, I had the chance to exchange ideas with people who see the world differently. What stayed with me were the questions worth thinking about long after those conversations ended.
A conversation. An idea. A beginning.
I’m Jacinth Jebaraj, a co-founder of Élan. I’m passionate about economics, business management and understanding how an idea becomes something people can be part of.

Élan began with a conversation between Akshit, our founder, and me as we walked back from lunch. What felt like an ordinary conversation became the starting point for something we would build together.

I enjoy exploring possibilities, learning from the people around me and taking that first step towards an idea. For me, Élan is a reminder of what can happen when people take an idea seriously and give it a chance to grow.

Sanjay Ghodawat International School is a co-educational
    international boarding school established in 2010 under the Sou. Sushila Danchand Ghodawat
    Charitable Trust. It runs campuses at Mulshi in Pune and at Atigre near Kolhapur, and the two
    operate as one institution across locations.

The school offers internationally recognised curricula, including
    the Cambridge programme and the International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme, alongside CBSE at
    the Kolhapur campus. SGIS Pune is a boarding school for students aged 6 to 18, set on a
    residential campus surrounded by greenery in Mulshi.

Beyond the classroom, SGIS runs an active programme in student
    leadership and global awareness, including a Model United Nations club where students train in
    public speaking, research and resolution writing, and take part in national and international
    conferences. Alongside this sit a wide range of co-curricular activities and sports, from swimming
    and rock-climbing to football, chess and athletics.

The school describes its approach as blending academic rigour with
    character education and real-world skills, rooted in integrity, empathy and resilience.

Information about the school is drawn from its official
    websites, and photographs are used with permission. For admissions or school enquiries, please
    contact SGIS directly rather than the Élan team.
Quad AI School of Technology and Management is the platinum sponsor of Élan Summit 2026.

Quad AI is an industry-first educational institution focused on making students
    career-ready. With a 100% placement focus, an industry-led curriculum, hands-on projects and
    mentorship from senior corporate leaders, it sets out to close the gap between education and
    employment.

The curriculum is curated by IIT, IIM, FMS and Harvard alumni, and sits alongside
    industry exposure, internships, entrepreneurship and personality development.

For participants making their own arrangements
The Early Bird, Standard and Late Registration passes include accommodation for the night of 5 September and transport in Pune between your accommodation and the venue. The

pass does not include accommodation or transport, and is for participants making their own arrangements. Travel to Pune itself is your own arrangement on every pass. Participants travelling from Kolhapur can travel with the Élan team at an additional charge, as the team travels from Kolhapur. Where accommodation is included, only one night’s stay is covered. Additional nights can be arranged at extra cost, but must be requested well in advance; requests made close to the event, or on the day, may not be possible.
